takeaway: The recurrent laryngeal nerve is closely related to the inferior thyroid artery, so it is at risk when that artery is ligated during a hemithyroidectomy.

lines.text: A 35-year-old woman is having a hemithyroidectomy.
lines.say: A thirty-five-year-old woman is having a hemi-thyroidectomy.

lines.text: Half of her thyroid gland is being removed.
To do this, the surgeon has to ligate the inferior thyroid artery.
But a tie placed here can catch a nerve lying close beside it.
That nerve is the recurrent laryngeal nerve.
Picture the artery as a road, with the nerve running right next to it.
The nerve is closely related to the inferior thyroid artery, so it is at risk whenever that artery is tied.
